subject: deepgram-full-20260913-1644
headline: While baseline latency beats industry benchmarks with excellent response quality, tail latency breaks under moderate concurrent load due to downstream thinking delays.

insights.title: Tail Latency Degrades Severely Under Load in refund-escalation Scenario
insights.finding: In the refund-escalation scenario, the median wait time remains stable under concurrency, but the p95 tail latency degrades heavily starting at 5 concurrent calls, failing the speed threshold.
insights.why_it_matters: A flat median alongside a ballooning p95 suggests that while typical calls are handled quickly, a significant portion of callers experience extreme queueing or delays, making the experience highly inconsistent.
insights.next_step: Investigate system concurrency limits and database lookup performance during the refund-escalation flow.

insights.title: Thinking and Processing is the Primary Latency Bottleneck
insights.finding: Outlier latency is caused almost entirely by the agent thinking and preparing its verbal response rather than network transmission or noticing when the caller stops talking.
insights.why_it_matters: Knowing the bottleneck is inside the thinking/speaking generation phase helps the team avoid wasting effort optimizing network connections or speech detection VAD thresholds.
insights.next_step: Profile LLM and speech generation performance under concurrent loads to reduce think-speak execution times.

insights.title: Test Harness Resource Exhaustion Invalidates Step Results
insights.finding: Multiple high-load steps are marked with a degraded test harness, which means the test infrastructure itself was overloaded, not necessarily the agent.
insights.why_it_matters: Drawing performance conclusions from degraded runs can lead to false architectural fixes or mask real performance bottlenecks.
insights.next_step: Upgrade the testing machine resources and repeat the high-concurrency steps to get clean measurements.

insights.title: Closing Turn (Turn 5) Has Consistently High Outlier Latency
evidence: refund-escalation, step baseline: turn 5 ttfa p95_ms 3150.9
refund-escalation, step baseline: turn 1 ttfa p95_ms 960.9
refund-bargein, step baseline: turn 5 ttfa p95_ms 3688.2
refund-bargein, step baseline: turn 1 ttfa p95_ms 1847.6
refund-branching, step baseline: turn 5 ttfa p95_ms 3205.3
refund-branching, step baseline: turn 1 ttfa p95_ms 1085.7
insights.finding: Across different runs, the final turn where the customer says goodbye or expresses thanks triggers significantly longer outlier delays than the opening turn.
insights.why_it_matters: A massive delay on the very last turn leaves callers hanging on a silent line right as they try to finish the call, leaving a poor final impression.
insights.next_step: Optimize prompt routing or context processing for final polite exchanges to ensure they return fast replies.

insights.title: Excellent Task Accuracy and Word Recognition Maintained Under Load
insights.finding: The agent maintains excellent conversational quality under load, with a baseline mean word error rate of 3.0% rising only slightly to 3.6% at c20.
insights.why_it_matters: The system successfully understands callers and executes requested jobs accurately (100.0% task success on judged calls) even when the system is heavily loaded.
insights.next_step: Preserve the active configuration of transcription and prompt logic, focusing strictly on speed optimization rather than accuracy fixes.

insights.title: Severe Systemic Delay in graph-reference Turn 4
evidence: graph-reference, step c20: turn 4 ttfa p50_ms 3151.1
graph-reference, step c20: turn 4 ttfa p95_ms 5448.7
insights.finding: In the graph-reference scenario, the final turn (Turn 4) displays extremely high median and outlier latency, exceeding 3 seconds for half of the callers.
insights.why_it_matters: A median of 3151.1 ms means almost every caller experiences a noticeable, uncomfortable multi-second gap of dead air, indicating a systemic logic bottleneck rather than an occasional glitch.
insights.next_step: Examine the backend operation or external integration running on Turn 4 in the graph-reference scenario to resolve the systemic 3-second block.
